added_failures_note: Measured: neither logs/baseline-suite.log nor logs/after-suite.log reports any FAILED or ERROR node id, so the set difference is empty. The same line-oriented extraction finds FAILED tests/test_summaries_list_live_and_recent_sprints.py::test_both_summaries_list_live_open_and_recently_closed in logs/negative-control-mutation.log, which is the positive control that the instrument reads a failure when one is present.

findings.text: CLOSED_SPRINT_STATUSES is assigned at module level twice - here as {done, shipped} and again at line 1645 as {done, shipped, closed, archived} - and the later binding wins, so sprint_summary_rows never sees the summary's own two-member set: an archived or closed sprint is treated as closed, dropped when it carries no close date and ordered into the recently-closed bucket instead of the open one, contrary to the section rule that every sprint not done or shipped is listed.

summary["sprints"] is an int count, set at line 2068, for a project with no qualifying sprint and a list of row dicts for a project with one, so a single field carries two shapes and a consumer reading the count breaks on exactly the projects that have sprints; the roadmap side avoided this by exposing the rows on a new summary_sprints key.

The head arm's header records revision 192aa9a4, the dispatch base, beside the tree label worktree(after), so the 148-passed count is not tied to the reviewed head 685657cbc by the reviewed run's own evidence; the same base sha is repeated as after_suite.revision in the manifest.

item_verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit against the base: cffc63fd5 carries the builder, the flight window key, the discovery call and the test; 685657cbc adds only the evidence fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done_when names a synthetic four-sprint ordering case and a response-budget reading; tests/test_summaries_list_live_and_recent_sprints.py:160 asserts the order on both surfaces and :206 asserts the budget, and the manifest records both results.
item_verdicts.goal: The node goal is that discovery and the roadmap summary both list open and recently closed sprints; reckon/mcp.py:2086 and reckon/roadmap.py:2831 feed one shared builder, and the head test asserts both surfaces return it.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read; it states 148 passed against a 143-passed baseline, names both gate logs and the negative-control log, and its stated totals reconcile with the logs it cites.
item_verdicts.write_paths: Read the manifest's declared paths; all six files in the diff sit inside them and nothing else changed between the base and the head.

justifications.durability: The declared mutation reddens tests/test_summaries_list_live_and_recent_sprints.py:164 as logs/negative-control-mutation.log records, but every fixture sprint is active, planned, done or shipped, so the rebound set at reckon/roadmap.py:1116 and the int arm of reckon/mcp.py:2094 are unguarded.
justifications.evidence: Both gate logs are on disk and end EXIT=0 with no FAILED or ERROR line, but the head arm's own header at logs/after-suite.log:1 records revision 192aa9a4, the dispatch base, beside the tree label worktree(after).
justifications.fit: reckon/roadmap.py:1116 reintroduces the module-level name CLOSED_SPRINT_STATUSES that reckon/roadmap.py:1645 already owns, and reckon/mcp.py:2094 leaves summary["sprints"] an int for a sprint-less project and a list otherwise, which is the two-shapes-for-one-read pattern this repository has already had to repair once.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The shared builder returns the declared row shape at reckon/roadmap.py:1236 and both surfaces call it, but reckon/roadmap.py:1116 is rebound at :1645, so an archived or closed sprint is windowed as closed instead of listed as open.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 192aa9a4 685657cbc names exactly the six declared write paths, and no figure directory was created under the declared figures path.
